summary.headline: Week ahead of target on both orders and revenue, with revenue at 113.6%; the year to date remains behind target at 96.3%.

points.what: Weekly gross revenue was $77,678, or 113.6% of the weekly target, and the brief marks the value as outside its 8-week range.
points.so_what: Revenue attainment ran ahead of orders attainment, so the week's beat came from order value as well as order count.

points.what: Orders came in at 980, down 1.5% week on week but up 84.6% on last year against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: The week still cleared its orders target despite the dip on the prior week.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 96.3% of the target to date, a shortfall of $57,991.
points.so_what: One week ahead of target does not move the year out of deficit.

points.what: The order cancellation rate fell 1.7 pp to 14.5%, rated good and flagged as a notable change.
points.so_what: Less of the week's order volume was lost before it converted to revenue, which supports the revenue attainment above.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue stands at 96.3% of target, and the remaining weeks require $84,333 a week against a current 8-week run-rate of $70,390.
points.so_what: At the recent pace the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: With one week left in 2026-Q2, $72,160 is still needed to reach the full-quarter target of $884,086, against an 8-week average weekly revenue of $68,426.
points.so_what: The quarter's slim surplus can only hold if the final week runs above the recent weekly pace.

points.what: New customer signups were down 11.4% on last year while orders were up 84.6%.
points.so_what: Customer additions are moving in the opposite direction to order growth, a risk to volume beyond this quarter.

points.what: Orders finished at 106.9% of the weekly target, 63 orders above it, and revenue at 113.6%, $9,300 above it.
points.so_what: The week added to the quarter's surplus rather than drawing it down.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $811,926, or 100.1% of the target for the same weeks, with one week left in the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter is only marginally ahead, so its outcome rests almost entirely on the final week.

points.what: Against the full-year target of $3,888,802, $2,361,319 remains with 28 weeks left.
points.so_what: Closing the year-to-date gap requires weekly revenue well above what recent weeks have delivered.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 18.0% to 137, a contribution of -30 orders and 200% of the total weekly change.
points.so_what: The week's orders decline sits with LATAM more than with any other region.

points.what: Search orders fell 6.1% to 683, contributing -44 orders, or 293.3% of the total change, while holding 69.7% of orders.
points.so_what: A decline in the largest source outweighed gains elsewhere and set the direction of total orders.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 16.4% to 192, contributing 27 orders, and Organic rose 21.1% to 161, contributing 28.
points.so_what: These gains offset most, but not all, of the losses in LATAM and Search.

points.what: Average order value rose 3.5% week on week to $92.69 and 4.0% on last year, and is flagged as outside its 8-week range.
points.so_what: Revenue grew on the week while orders fell, so the gain came from value per order rather than volume.

points.what: The cancellation rate of 14.5% is 0.2 pp below last year, and each percentage point of cancellations is worth $908 of revenue.
points.so_what: The improvement in cancellations added close to a thousand dollars of revenue relative to the prior week's rate.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 01 Jun 2026 was 9.4%, up 0.1 pp on the week before and 0.2 pp on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns are edging up in both comparisons, which erodes the value of the revenue reported gross of returns.

points.what: New customer signups were 241, down 0.4% on the prior week.
points.so_what: Signups have flattened at a level below last year, so order growth is not being matched by account growth.
